title: docs: document complete bans and the unban trap
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
Banning 22 card testers today surfaced three things the skill did not say.

- **A ban is three statements, not one.** Setting `banned = 1` alone leaves the session live and auto top-up still charging. Documents the full set from `fraudBanQueries()`, plus expiring open Checkout sessions and what to verify after.
- **Unbanning has a trap.** Clearing `banned` on an account the payment-fraud job can see gets it re-banned within the hour unless the id also goes into `FRAUD_BAN_EXCLUDED_USER_IDS`.
- **Payment-fraud bans work differently** from the abuse scoring already in the skill: hourly review queue posting to Discord, enforcement off by default, a confirmed signal required, and charges before 2026-05-01 unattributable so those accounts need manual review.

Also corrects the enforcement file path (`shared/auth/api-key.ts`, not `src/middleware/auth.ts`) and adds today's action to the log.

Docs only.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

gist.headline: The Unban Snare Is Mapped
gist.blurb: The abuse-detection field guide now documents that a ban takes three actions, not one. It also marks the spot where an unban can quietly grow right back.
gist.summary: Expanded the abuse-detection skill with the complete fraud-ban procedure: set `banned = 1`, expire open Checkout sessions, stop auto top-ups, verify enforcement, and add unbanned payment-fraud accounts to `FRAUD_BAN_EXCLUDED_USER_IDS` to prevent hourly re-bans.
gist.impact: Moderators now have a concrete runbook for handling payment-fraud bans, including the confirmed-signal requirement, Discord review queue, manual review for charges before 2026-05-01, and the corrected `shared/auth/api-key.ts` enforcement path.
